small_guidance:
- Add larger BLOCK_P configs (512, 1024) since total_pooled = 8*16*16 = 2048 per (N,OC); fewer iterations of the outer loop reduces overhead. Try num_warps=8/16 with num_stages=2.
- Hoist the per-(od,oh,ow) input gather: with stride=2 and pad=1, only ~half the (kd,kh,kw) combos satisfy id_r==0; use tl.static_range with compile-time-known parity selection so the masked loads collapse, and reorder loops so the IC reduction is innermost vectorized via tl.dot-style accumulation.
- Precompute and pass MK^3 as constexpr and unroll only valid (kd,kh,kw) parity combinations (KD_eff=2 per dim) — current kernel iterates 3^3=27 cells but only ~8 yield valid input; restructure to skip the always-invalid ones at compile time.
large_guidance:
- Switch from "one program per (N, OC)" gather to a scatter-add formulation: one program per (N, IC, input-spatial tile) writes the input×kernel outer product into a workspace conv output, then a second small kernel does scale+maxpool+gap+clamp. The current kernel recomputes the same input values redundantly across pooled positions; scatter amortizes input loads (3-channel input is tiny vs. 16-channel output).
- Alternatively, fuse but tile over output channels too: one program per (N, output-spatial tile) computing all OC=16 at once via a GEMM (BLOCK_OC=16, BLOCK_SPATIAL=tile), reusing the loaded input voxel across all OC. This turns the inner IC*K^3 loop into a (IC*K^3)×OC matmul with shared input loads.
- Persistent kernel over (N*OC) with channels_last input layout so IC=3 loads coalesce; combined with smaller pooled grid PD*PH*PW=2048 fitting in registers, a single-pass reduction avoids the outer BLOCK_P loop entirely (set BLOCK_P=2048).
